How could you do that at all?

You are to blame for everything yourself.
Nobody discussed the banquet with me.
I will definitely fire you for this!
But under the contract you cannot.
What was that on stage just now?
Try our new hot dish!

words.gram: masculine accusative singular inanimate demonstrative pronoun

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: This simply cannot be happening!
Just call and tell him.
I just did not try hard enough yesterday.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('little').

examples.trans: Oh, just one small trifle.
I only want a small piece.
This is just a little joke!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'joke, prank' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is just a little joke!
It's a joke.
What kind of jokes are these?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'юрприз'). Common masculine noun meaning 'surprise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это сюрприз от нашего усатого клоуна.
examples.trans: It is a surprise from our mustachioed clown.
I'll show you one surprise.
What surprise?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I work right here for you.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.
And did you ever think of me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.
Our head cook there got sick.

examples.text: Нам нужно решить нашу деликатную проблему.
examples.trans: We need to solve our delicate problem.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'сатый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('mustachioed').

examples.text: Это сюрприз от нашего усатого клоуна.
examples.trans: It is a surprise from our mustachioed clown.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень усатый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very mustachioed choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'from the clown' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это сюрприз от нашего усатого клоуна.
examples.trans: It is a surprise from our mustachioed clown.
A clown works at the circus.
Don't be a clown!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I still have to inspect the whole hotel.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('very much, big').

examples.text: Но он больше музыкант, чем повар.
examples.trans: But he is more of a musician than a cook.

examples.text: А я недавно большой кредит взял.
examples.trans: And I recently took out a big loan.

examples.text: У неё в этом опыта больше.
examples.trans: She has more experience in that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, here is the key card for you.
Thank you all very much for your attention.
Thanks, Dad!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you all very much for your attention.
May I have your attention.
Thank you for your attention.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Why did you kill that snake?
What have you come for?
What's that for?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And did you ever think of me?
There were difficult moments in life.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'snake' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нагиев совсем не изменился за это время!
examples.trans: Nagiyev has not changed at all during this time!
Many people consider snakes very cute.

examples.text: Но на змею придётся сегодня скинуться.
examples.trans: But we will have to chip in for the snake today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'killed', paired with 'убивать'.

examples.trans: Wait, did you kill my Arkady?!
Why did you kill that snake?
Do you want to kill me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как тебе работать у бывшей жены?
examples.trans: How is it working for your ex-wife?

examples.text: Ой, как же мне сейчас больно!
examples.trans: Oh, how much that hurts right now!

examples.text: Кто, как не мы, поддержит природу?
examples.trans: Who if not we will support nature?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.

examples.text: Я русский язык вообще не знаю.
examples.trans: I do not know the Russian language at all.

examples.text: Как ты вообще мог это сделать?
examples.trans: How could you do that at all?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: Denis, can you help me, please?
I can't today.
That can't be.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: The chef built this wonderful restaurant.
Do it by any means necessary.

examples.text: Как ты вообще мог это сделать?
examples.trans: How could you do that at all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вспомнили, что у вас есть дочь?
examples.trans: Did you remember that you have a daughter?

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.
Victor Petrovich, what happened?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Чтобы вкусно её для вас приготовить.
examples.trans: In order to cook it deliciously for you.
It's delicious!
Mum is a good cook.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она ничего об этом не знала.
examples.trans: She knew nothing about it.

examples.text: Она выгонит нас, чтобы вас унизить.
examples.trans: She will kick us out to humiliate you.

examples.text: За что она хотела меня уволить?
examples.trans: Why did she want to fire me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: These are rare animals for the evening.
We were collecting money for them.

examples.text: Чтобы вкусно её для вас приготовить.
examples.trans: In order to cook it deliciously for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?
You are under my roof now.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!
examples.trans: I need to step outside for fresh air urgently!

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, cook', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Чтобы вкусно её для вас приготовить.
examples.trans: In order to cook it deliciously for you.

examples.text: Только вы же сами её приготовили!
examples.trans: But you cooked it yourself!
I cooked an ordinary eel today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?
I work right here for you.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'myself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not be afraid, you will manage on your own.
Blow into this tube yourself.
To that same cursed room.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('guilty / at fault').

examples.trans: You are to blame for everything yourself.
It's your fault!

examples.text: Я ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: I'm not to blame for anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nobody here will touch you.
Then do not be in a hurry.
Nobody is going to fire you here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'banquet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Никто со мной банкет не обсуждал.
examples.trans: Nobody discussed the banquet with me.
A festive banquet.

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'суждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'discussed', paired with 'обсудить'.

examples.text: Никто со мной банкет не обсуждал.
examples.trans: Nobody discussed the banquet with me.
Don't discuss, act!
Well, we've been discussing everything here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Thank you, here is the key card for you.
And also our Far Eastern rat snake.

examples.text: Я тебя за это точно уволю!
examples.trans: I will definitely fire you for this!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will fire', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: They just fired me.
Who fired you?
Nobody is going to fire you here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.
Excuse me, I need to go.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!
examples.trans: I need to step outside for fresh air urgently!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'according to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

examples.text: Очень хорошо, и к Кате поближе.
examples.trans: Very good, and closer to Katya.

meanings.note: From Latin 'contractus' (agreement, drawing together, from 'contrahere').

examples.text: По контракту только я могу увольнять.
examples.trans: Under the contract, only I can fire cooks.

examples.text: Но по контракту ты не можешь.
examples.trans: But under the contract you cannot.
My military contract ended.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вспомнили, что у вас есть дочь?
examples.trans: Did you remember that you have a daughter?

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.
Victor Petrovich, what happened?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Vitya, meet her right now.

examples.text: Сейчас попрощаемся, выпьем, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.
And where are you going right now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: This simply cannot be happening!

examples.text: Завтра шеф должен быть на больничном.
examples.trans: Tomorrow the chef must be on sick leave.

examples.text: Я очень хочу быть с Катей.
examples.trans: I really want to be with Katya.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Yes, I already know that.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'цена'). Common feminine noun meaning 'the stage' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Go ahead and read your script.

examples.text: Что это сейчас было на сцене?
examples.trans: What was that on stage just now?

examples.text: А на сцену выходит — превращается в дерево.
examples.trans: But when she goes out on stage, she turns into a tree.

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.
I'll try one more time.
Let's try.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: У неё на новом месте всё в порядке.
examples.trans: Everything is fine with her at the new place.
Mom, please stop him!

examples.text: Старый кредит отдам и новый возьму.
examples.trans: I will pay off the old loan and take a new one.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Try our new hot dish!
Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I love you. Do not miss me too much.
It is a dish that is served cold.
Try our new hot dish!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will answer', paired with 'отвечать'.

examples.text: Нагиев мне за рыбку ещё ответит!
examples.trans: Nagiyev will pay me back for my little fish!

examples.text: Ты мне ответишь за этот скандал!
examples.trans: You will answer to me for this scandal!
I have to answer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'кандал'). Common masculine noun meaning 'scandal, fuss, row' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты мне ответишь за этот скандал!
examples.trans: You will answer to me for this scandal!
A scandal began in the restaurant dining room.
There is no need to make a scene.
